sam.j: quick q — ran into a weird mismatch between py/ts SDKs and the REST contract on the `stop_sequences` param. python client omits it when None, ts client sends `stopSequences: []`, and the REST handler treats empty list differently from missing. can we align?

tasha: oof. do you have a minimal repro? which endpoint?

sam.j: /v1/generate. repro: py sdk call `client.generate(prompt, stop_sequences=None)` => payload has no `stop_sequences` key. ts sdk call `client.generate({ prompt, stopSequences: undefined })` -> after JSON.stringify it ends up as `"stopSequences":[]` due to our helper. REST expects missing vs empty list to mean different things (missing = default model behavior, empty list = disable all stops).

kevin_w: that sounds like two separate problems: naming casing + defaulting semantics. ts->rest camelCase mapping should translate `stopSequences` -> `stop_sequences` and drop undefined. but the helper that coerces arrays is converting undefined -> [] somewhere.

ci-bot: CI check: serializer/unit-tests failed on PR #1287 — see https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1287/checks — failure in ts-serializer spec (undefined -> [])

sam.j: here's snippet:```js
// TS call
client.generate({ prompt: 'hi', stopSequences: undefined })
// serialized body we see: {"prompt":"hi","stopSequences":[]}
```
```py
# PY call
client.generate('hi', stop_sequences=None)
# serialized body: {"prompt":"hi"}
```

tasha: thanks. I think py uses `omit_none=True` in our json encoder, ts relies on a `cleanup` util that should remove undefined but currently normalizes arrays. I'll open a small PR to change cleanup to not coerce arrays.

kevin_w: +1. also add a casing layer so SDKs share a central name map. otherwise we'll keep getting `stopSequences` vs `stop_sequences` bugs. Proposed change: map camelCase -> snake_case at top-level keys, then run omitUndefined/omitNone. That order keeps semantics clear.

sam.j: can we also add an integration test that compares SDK->REST payload equivalence for a few edge cases: undefined vs null vs [] vs omitted? caught me earlier.

ci-bot: test suggestion: add param matrix in `sdk/integration/serializers/test_matrix.ts` and `pytests/test_serializers.py`.

kevin_w: I'll draft PR that: 1) fixes cleanup behavior (don't coerce undefined arrays), 2) introduces mapping util, 3) adds integration tests. Will ping when ready for review.

sam.j: thanks. one more subtlety — server-side currently treats empty list as explicit "no stops" which some customers relied on. we should preserve that semantics — so change must ensure SDKs can still send [] when caller intentionally sets stops: [] vs omit when None/undefined.

kevin_w: yep — plan: only coerce when caller explicitly passes `stopSequences: []` (keep that), but if it's undefined we remove the key. update changelog + note in SDK migration guide.

kevin_w: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1302 (WIP) -- tests added, serializer changes.

ci-bot: build queued for #1302.

deploy-bot: reminder: feature branch tests may take longer during scheduled infra maintenance (today 22:00-23:30 UTC).

sam.j: awesome — will wait for the PR, then run the downstream service tests. thanks all :thumbsup:

tasha: thanks — also adding a short note to the SDK release notes about `stop_sequences` behavior and param naming quirks so SDK consumers don't get surprised.
